subject: english
question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

Don’t go to the neighbour’s garden, ______ not allowed to go there.
solution:
The correct answer is **"you're".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The blank in the sentence **"Don’t go to the neighbour’s garden, ________ not allowed to go there." **is meant to indicate a contraction for **'you are'. **
 
• **​**The sentence is basically saying **"You are not allowed to go there."**
 
• **"You’re" **is a contraction of **'you are', **which communicates the intended meaning perfectly in this context.
 
 
• **Example**: *You need to wear seat belts when **you're**__ in the car.*
 
 
 
• Hence, filling the blank with **"you're" **will complete the sentence correctly as: **"Don’t go to the neighbour’s garden, you’re not allowed to go there."**
 
• So, the correct answer is **"Option 4."**

 

**Correct sentence: ***Don’t go to the neighbour’s garden, __**you're**__ not allowed to go there.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__

 
• Analyzing the other options:

 
 
• "your" is a possessive adjective, used before a noun to show something that belongs to "you", which doesn't fit this context.
 
• "yore" is a noun that refers to times long past and doesn't make sense in this context.
 
• "yor" is not a recognized English word, so it's not a suitable option.
